content: The provided text is a detailed schedule of interviews and presentations at the American Heart Association (AHA) 2010 conference. On Saturday, November 13, 2010, the following sessions are scheduled: 1:15 PM 1:45 PM: Dr. Adrian F. Hernandez, Dr. Christopher M. O'Connor, and Dr. Randy Starling will discuss the Acute Study of Clinical Effectiveness of Nesiritide in Decompensated Heart Failure Trial (ASCEND-HF). The embargo on this study lifts at 5:23 PM on Sunday, November 14, 2010. 1:45 PM 2:15 PM: Dr. Clyde Yancy will provide a historical perspective on the ASCEND trial and its implications for patient care. 3:15 PM 3:45 PM: Dr. Manesh Patel, Dr. Ken Mahaffey, and Dr. Keith Fox will present findings from the Stroke Prevention Using the Oral Direct Factor Xa Inhibitor Rivaroxaban Compared with Warfarin in Patients with Nonvalvular Atrial Fibrillation (ROCKET AF) trial. The embargo lifts at 10:55 AM on Monday, November 15, 2010. 3:45 PM 4:15 PM: Dr. Zubin Eapen will share insights on the AHA 2010 conference from a cardiology fellow's perspective. 4:30 PM 5:00 PM: Dr. Christopher M. O'Connor and Dr. Robert Harrington will discuss Duke University's presence at AHA, including ongoing activities and expectations. On Sunday, November 14, 2010, the following sessions are scheduled: 1:00 PM 1:30 PM: Dr. Deepak Voora will present findings from a study on a whole blood RNA signature that classifies multiple measures of platelet function on aspirin in healthy volunteers. The embargo lifts at 3:15 PM on Monday, November 15, 2010. 1:30 PM 2:00 PM: Dr. Kenneth Ellenbogen will discuss the primary results of the ADVANCE Bridge to Transplant Trial, which compares different programming strategies in cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). The embargo lifts at 4:39 PM on Monday, November 15, 2010. 2:00 PM 2:30 PM: Dr. David Cohen will present on health-related quality of life outcomes following transcatheter aortic valve implantation versus non-surgical therapy in inoperable patients with severe aortic stenosis, based on results from the PARTNER Trial (Cohort B). The embargo lifts at 4:55 PM on Monday, November 15, 2010. 2:30 PM 3:00 PM: Dr. Jonathan Piccini will discuss the association of sustained ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation with increased arrhythmic and all-cause mortality following non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndromes. The embargo lifts at 12:00 PM on Wednesday, November 17, 2010. 3:00 PM 3:30 PM: Dr. Thomas Povsic will present findings from a pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic substudy of RB006, a direct Factor IX inhibitor, in patients with acute coronary syndromes. The embargo lifts at 11:00 AM on Tuesday, November 16, 2010. On Monday, November 15, 2010, the following sessions are scheduled: 9:00 AM 9:30 AM: Dr. Christoph Kaiser will discuss late cardiac death and myocardial infarction associated with late stent thrombosis in large vessel stenting, comparing firstand second-generation drug-eluting stents to bare-metal stents. This is part of the BASKET PROVE study. The embargo lifts at 11:39 AM on Tuesday, November 16, 2010. 9:30 AM 10:00 AM: Karen S. Pieper will present insights from the PLATO trial, focusing on the use of proton pump inhibitors as a marker for cardiovascular risk rather than a causative factor. The embargo lifts at 9:15 AM on Tuesday, November 16, 2010. 10:00 AM 10:30 AM: Dr. Kristin Newby will provide updates on the MURDOCK study and discuss challenges and opportunities in biomarker research. 10:30 AM 11:00 AM: Prof. Murray Esler will present findings from the SYMPLICITY HTN-2 trial, an international, multicenter, randomized controlled trial evaluating renal sympathetic denervation for hypertension treatment. The embargo lifts at 12:01 PM on Wednesday, November 17, 2010. On Tuesday, November 16, 2010, the following sessions are scheduled: 9:00 AM 9:30 AM: Dr. Sunil Rao will present the primary results of the REVEAL trial, a randomized placebo-controlled study of intravenous erythropoietin to reduce infarct size after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. The embargo lifts at 4:10 PM on Monday, November 15, 2010. 9:30 AM 10:00 AM: Dr. Stephen J. Nicholls will discuss the first major clinical trial of an oral agent inducing ApoA1 synthesis, a novel approach to HDL raising and cardiovascular risk modification. The embargo lifts at 11:39 AM on Wednesday, November 17, 2010. This format provides a clear, professional summary of the schedule while maintaining the detailed information about each session, including embargo times and trial specifics.
